#1320. Harry Kane proves there is only one Ballon d’Or winner

Let’s cut to the chase. If there is any justice, sanity or logic in football then Harry Kane will win the Ballon d’Or when the ceremony takes place in London on Monday.

Arsenal would have deservedly won this Champions League match away to Bayern Munich if Kane was not on the pitch. Instead, they almost lost it but for another bit of brilliance from Declan Rice, Kane’s vice-captain for England, and probably his successor to wear the armband.

A brilliantly worked team-goal finished off by Declan Rice, and Arsenal are level 💥 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/Y25zI80A0z

“I’m lucky I can play with him and not so lucky I have to play against him,” Rice said, and that summed it up succinctly.

And that Ballon d’Or? There is bias, but Rice – who is also on the 30-strong list of nominees – added of Kane: “He is the clear winner. His numbers speak for themselves, the year he has had has been remarkable. When you play with him you realise how good he is and when you play against him you see how much of a pain it is.”

Arsenal stood toe-to-toe with Bayern in an open match. Both sides went for it, partly because they knew under the Champions League format, that defeat was not a disaster. There has been some chat about whether Arsenal can be, well, a bit dull. Not here. It would be no surprise to see these two face off again deep into this competition.

The only setback for Arsenal was a worrying injury to Bukayo Saka early on, limping off and tapping his thigh, indicating an issue with his muscle. Mikel Arteta’s reaction betrayed his understandable concern.

Kane won a penalty and then expertly took it to give Bayern the lead. Other strikers could have scored the penalty but few would have created the wonderful assist that drew Bayern level.

It has been a fact for quite some years that Kane is not only the best goalscorer for England but the best passer. Indeed, if Kane could provide for Kane he would have scored even more goals.

“Unsere nummer neun,” shouted the stadium announcer after Kane’s goal and that needed no translation. Kane is a god in Bavaria, where they know a few things about having great centre-forwards. But the 33-year-old is surpassing them all.

Kane’s goal meant he had scored in 10 straight Champions League games, one short of the record held by Cristiano Ronaldo. It was also the former Tottenham Hotspur forward’s 16th goal in 23 games against Arsenal. No one has ever scored more against them.

Kane is the complete player, carrying out his defensive duties – winning headers to clear Bayern’s lines from Arsenal free-kicks – to linking the play to being the focus of his team’s attacks. He is a centre-half, central midfielder and centre-forward. Who pops up on the wing to deliver pinpoint crosses.

Maybe Kane will be pipped at the Palladium – the theatre where the ceremony takes place – by Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal or Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappé, or even an absurd sympathy vote for Lionel Messi. But Kane deserves it. His time is now.

Some passages of play in the first half deserve analysis. Just to highlight how good Kane was. After an Arsenal corner, wastefully volleyed over by Riccardo Calafiori, Bayern countered and suddenly it was three on two. Serge Gnabry, the former Arsenal winger, had to do better than shoot weakly when picked out on the overlap. David Raya saved. That was a let-off.

But who sprung that counter? It was not Manuel Neuer, the Bayern goalkeeper, taking the goal-kick, but Kane, with his sharp thinking. And then Kane launched a superb pass from deep which Ismael Saibari should have dealt with better. It should have been another opportunity. Potentially a goal.

Is there anything Harry Kane can't do? 🧐 His goal kick very nearly led to a Bayern Munich goal 😲 https://t.co/fqbsN7KOjw

And then Bayern did score. The ball was played inside to Kane, in centre field and afforded too much space. He delivered a perfectly weighted through ball for Alphonse Davies to run on to. The pace was perfect, allowing the Canadian not to break stride and stroke it past Raya. Kane did not fire the ball in, he did not make Davies work to reach it and he did not give Jurrien Timber any chance of cutting it out. It was perfect. Few players could do that. “Harry Kane puts the ball in a space from 30 metres that doesn’t exist,” Arteta said. True.

Harry Kane with an OUTRAGEOUS assist, and Alphonso Davies equalises 🥵 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/6cGXrUloHW

It was Saka’s replacement who gave Arsenal the lead, Eberechi Eze profiting from Martin Odegaard’s perceptive, lofted pass and taking advantage of Bayern’s ragged defending and some suspect goalkeeping from 40-year-old Neuer to score from an angle. Initially it was ruled out for offside, but that was overturned after a VAR check to provide Eze with a bit of redemption after being hooked against Nottingham Forest at the weekend.

VAR has given it, and Eze strikes Arsenal into the lead at the Allianz 🔥 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/i1LjrZVnbI

Neuer had his own slice of redemption as he saved well from Bruno Guimarães’ close-range header, pushing it against a post with Raya also excelling to beat out another header, this time from Dayot Upamecano.

When Timber was punished for handball, as he blocked Kane’s shot, the penalty was given. Up stepped Kane and we knew the rest. At that point it felt like Bayern would win, but Arsenal continued to play courageously and pushed on, as they had done throughout, risking conceding further goals.

Harry Kane, what a penalty 🥶 He scores in his TENTH consecutive Champions League game to give Bayern the lead 😳 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/4k4jPCQEWF

They were rewarded as Rice started the move, playing the ball in quickly to Noni Madueke with substitute Viktor Gyokeres laying it back into the midfielder’s path. He strode on and Neuer was again beaten from an angle. It was certainly warranted, even if it did not detract from Kane’s night. But will he have a greater one on Monday?

It had similarities [with last year’s league phase game]. I think we managed to create more chances but I think that Arsenal – and it’s something that has been mentioned by them before the game – they’ve worked a lot on retaining the ball and making it difficult to get the ball back. We did feel that.

It was a game in chunks. They had moments, we had moments. In our moments, I think we exploited the spaces in behind a little bit better maybe but we played against a top team and the result is a result between two big teams.

Last year they reaped the benefits of a top-two finish: home ties all the way to the final and a guarantee of avoiding the other club in the top two.

They have a chance to pick off Real Madrid at the Emirates, and will anticipate Aston Villa (who still have to play Barcelona and PSG) and Real Betis dropping points.

Given PSG have already dispatched Manchester City and Barcelona, it is hard to envisage them dropping a point, though they do have the odd off night.

Arsenal’s chances of grabbing second could come down to winning their remaining games and Liverpool slipping up. But with five games to go, these permutations are probably premature.

Wow, what a game. That is one of the highest levels that we have played. The level of opposition, what the game required, and our level as well. Two teams who wanted to press each other and wanted to attack and wanted to play. It was a fascinating game.

I think we started the game incredibly well, we were so dominant, we did everything to deserve the first goal. We didn’t score the goal and lost Bukayo and had to adapt to it.

We gave a terrible chance away after our corner which could have cost us, then we scored the goal. In the second half, the game was even,  they started probably a little bit better before they scored and they you have to react and we certainly did.

The spirit of the team, the quality we have showed on the second goal as well.

They are a bit concerned. A player having to come off with a sharp pain is never good news but we have to wait and see.

For me he’s the clear winner, his numbers speak for themselves. He’s obviously up against some other world class players. When you play with him you see how good it is, and when you play against him you see how much of a pain he is! As a striker to play that pass for the goal... he’s ridiculous. Lucky I can play with him, not so lucky when I have to play against him.

I thought it was a good performance. Probably the draw was a fair result overall. We probably just didn’t get quite enough right tonight to get the win.

Nice to get the assist to get back into the game and then I thought we had some good moments but not enough over the 90 minutes.

When you play against teams like Bayern who are man to man all over the pitch you have to apply certain principles, and I just kept running and managed to get away from my man. When they are following you all over, I just kept running and I was in on the goal.

He’s been making such a good impact from the bench [Gyokeres]. He’s made some great runs tonight and set me up for the goal. When you play against man to man, who follow you everywhere over the whole pitch, it’s such a tough game. You have to apply certain principles and concepts, and you’re constantly thinking about where the space is. For the goal, Noni one-touch set, Viktor’s one-touch set, those little movements put you through on goal.

In periods of the game, it felt like Arsenal were trying to play in the manner of Bayern or PSG by leaving themselves so light at the back with acres of green grass to cover.

Would they play like that in a quarter-final? Probably not, and they were emboldened by Bayern missing some key players. But it helped them create danger and have some strong spells, even if there were some scary moments going the other way.

Somewhere between that display and Arsenal’s rearguard in the Champions League final is probably the sweet spot.

A high-quality game between two of the most plausible winners of this season’s Champions League finishes level.

It was a helter-skelter contest at times. For all the talk of Arteta being a conservative coach, Arsenal committed numbers forward in their press and when they attacked, and that left them vulnerable to Bayern’s fast transitions and Kane’s passes from deep.

Perhaps it is a missed opportunity to beat Bayern in the Allianz, given the German side started without Olise, Kimmich, Musiala and Diaz, but a point from the hardest fixture of the league phase is more than acceptable.

The fly in the ointment is the injury suffered by Saka in the first half, but Eze and Madueke performed well in his absence.

Just one minute to play and Bayern have the ball in Arsenal’s half, but Calafiori gets his foot in. Madueke does well to keep it and Lewis-Skelly finds Eze.

Timber with dig from outside the box after a poor defensive header from Bayern, and Neuer tips it over. Rice to take the corner, and Arsenal’s set-pieces have caused problems throughout. This might just be Arsenal’s chance to win it.

Swung to the back post, but Tah did enough.

Bayern had an injury worry of their own now: Luis Diaz, not judged fit to start, has pulled up and will have to come off. Bayern were in a promising position in the Arsenal half.

Harry Kane looking for another of those arced passes forward, but Eze read it and retrieved. Arsenal finishing the stronger when it comes to possession and territory. Perhaps that Premier League intensity bearing fruit as the game progresses.

A couple of fouls given away by both teams, it has been a bitty few minutes. But Arsenal do well to find Lewis-Skelly free in the middle of the pitch, and he finds Rice who drives the away team forward.

Neither team appears inclined to settle for the draw, but Arsenal have the wind in their sails. Mikel Merino is on for Martin Odegaard, who has probably been Arsenal’s best player on the night.

Arsenal back level again, and it is an emphatic finish across Neuer from Rice, after a deft touch from Gyokeres around the corner at the edge of the box. Bright football around the box from Arsenal. Still 10 minutes or so to play.

Arsenal have been scoring gorgeous team goals all season. They have done so in all three of their Champions League games this season. They were labelled as “boring” after the Forest victory but that game was the exception, rather than the rule, on the evidence of this campaign.

A brilliantly worked team-goal finished off by Declan Rice, and Arsenal are level 💥 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/Y25zI80A0z

Arsenal deep in Bayern territory after Rice’s cross towards Eze glanced off the head of a defender. Bayern are keeping a good defensive shape though, Arsenal finding it difficult to penetrate. Arteta is preparing another pair of changes.

Luis Diaz with a snap shot that brings a sharp save from David Raya. On the balance of chances and threat created, Bayern have earned their lead. But still plenty of football to play. Arsenal have not scored from a set-piece this season, but they have looked dangerous tonight. They need another couple.

Neuer has just smashed into Stanisic, sweeping up a long ball Timber was chasing.

With Tzolis out and Saka now likely to be joining him on the sidelines, at what point does Arteta turn to Dowman in the league and Champions League? Obviously there are so many physical and defensive demands that are very difficult for a 16-year-old to meet... but the talent is there.

Arsenal enjoying plenty of territory and possession now, but you’d say Bayern look more likely to score on the counter-attack. Arsenal content to keep the ball and set themselves for a late assault.

Lewis-Skelly with a no-touch turn in midfield but then he takes too long and Bischof wins the ball cleanly. Davies nutmegs Rice on the counter, but Madueke tracked back diligently to snuff out the danger. At the other end, Karl fouls Eze who has enjoyed a strong game, aside from his goal.

Karl and Diaz are on for Bayern, replacing Gnarby and Saibari. If anything that shifts Bayern up a gear. Arteta has also made a double change: Lewis-Skelly on for Guimaraes, and Gyokeres on for Havertz.

The more open and transitional this game has become, the less comfortable Arsenal have looked. I’m not surprised Arteta has taken off Guimarães, as they have been struggling in that midfield battle for much of this second half. It feels like Bayern have taken this game to a place that Arsenal did not quite want to go: lots of space, lots of running, lots of interchanging positions.

Laimer with a foul on Eze near the left-corner of the penalty area, so Arsenal have a free-kick in a promising position for a cross. Havertz, Konsa, Gabriel and Timber the targets.

Brilliant deliver from Odeegard, somehow Arsenal fail to apply the finishing touch from a few yards out.

Bayern then escape and stream forward on the break, and Laimer snaps a shot wide.

Arsenal looking a little shaken at the back after conceding the goal, but Raya is fouled from the corner which helps them clear their lines. Luis Diaz is about to come on for the home team.

Bayern Munich lead for the first time on the night. Kane with a short stutter, before sending Raya the wrong way and wrapping the shot into the back of the net with power.

Harry Kane, what a penalty 🥶 He scores in his TENTH consecutive Champions League game to give Bayern the lead 😳 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/4k4jPCQEWF

Laimer’s pull back deflected into the path of Harry Kane, and Timber had his arm raised as he slid in to make the block. The referee wasted no time to give the penalty, and there are few complaints. Kane with the chance to score a ninth penalty against Arsenal. Raya up against him.

Bruno Guimaraes and Odegaard with some silky touches to help Arsenal win a free-kick in midfield. Arteta has some of his subs warming up, though he has already used one with Saka going off early on.

Arsenal close to a second goal again, after neat football involving Guimaraes and Havertz to release Eze on the left, and Neuer stuck out a leg to help Bayern scramble the ball away. It would be a surprise if this finished 1-1.

That’s a few times in this game that Arsenal have been ripped open after all going forward for a corner. It’s very uncharacteristic for Arteta’s side, who are usually so solid in their defensive shape.

The game continues to be very open, but some of that is the quality on show from both teams. Will Arteta call off the dogs at some point and tell his players to sit off in a defensive shape, or will they keep swinging punches?

Now Raya makes a world-class save at the other end! Upamecano skipped through the Arsenal press and there was acres of space to exploit again. Gnabry stood up a cross to the back post and Raya made a point-black save from Saibari’s header. It looked like he had to score from six yards.

What a save from Neuer! Down low to keep out a Guimaraes header from the corner. He was reaching back to the goal-line and he plucked the ball up on to the bar.

Arsenal were then stretched on the counter, but Saibari was offside.

Kane almost produced another great through ball within 30 seconds of the restart, but Gabriel made an interception. Arsenal need Bruno Guimaraes to be on the ball, on a couple of occasions he has been caught in space when Bayern come forward.

Arsenal respond though, and Arsenal win a corner through Eze.

Tah replaces Kim at centre-back, so a like for like change.

Arteta will be very disappointed by how Bayern were able to find Kane free in the middle from a throw-in. Whether Konsa should have been higher or Madueke further across, it was too simple.

A high-wire act from both teams, who are pushing numbers forward with and without the ball. Lots of man-to-man duels all over the pitch, and when one is lost there is loads of space to exploit. It has made for an entertaining half, and 1-1 is a fair scoreline. Arsenal controlled the first 25 to 30 minutes, but Bayern have looked dangerous.

The bigger story for Arsenal is the thigh injury suffered by Saka. It would be very surprising to see him before the November international break, at best. He pulled up abruptly.

Lovely Bayern move, whenever they reach three or four passes against Arsenal’s man-to-man pressure they have runners flying forward. Gnabry takes on a shot from a tight angle, and it deflects behind for a corner. Raya does well to claim.

Alphonso Davies’ pace is causing Arsenal some problems, and now it is Bayern’s turn to have a corner. Arsenal have lost some of their control of the first 30 minutes, but still look dangerous themselves. Timber is fouled from the corner, Arsenal free-kick.

Odegaard with a poor pass in the middle of the park, but Konsa produced a tremendous block to stop Kane’s left-footed shot across Raya.

Within 10 seconds, Arsenal are at the edge of the Bayern box through Rice and they win a corner after Eze’s shot was blocked.

The corner is flicked to the back post, where Calafiori was inches away from scoring from six inches out. Close to Arsenal’s first set-piece goal of the season.

The game is stretched now and quite entertaining, a very different feel to Arsenal’s Premier League assignments. Konsa realised Arsenal were short of numbers and lunged in against Harry Kane, hacking him down at the expense of a booking. Rice and his team-mates recovered well against the counter in any case.

Kane with another superb pass, perfectly curled around Timber into the path of Alphonso Davies who finishes beyond Raya. Kane had too much space in the middle of the pitch, Madueke perhaps guilty of not narrowing in.

Kane has played some absolutely absurd passes in this first half and that was the best yet. Alphonso Davies is so quick that Arsenal were never going to catch him, and the pass was so good that David Raya could not come to it.

Harry Kane with an OUTRAGEOUS assist, and Alphonso Davies equalises 🥵 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/6cGXrUloHW

A word of warning for Arsenal is that Kompany has Lennart Karl and Luis Diaz sat on his bench. At least one of those attackers will be on at half-time unless something changes.

Arsenal winning most of the aerial battles and duels for second balls at the moment, Bayern not building any pressure or fluency. There has been the odd flash of danger when Kane flips a pass in behind but Arteta’s team are comfortable at the moment.

Odegaard almost finds Eze with a lovely disguised through ball.

There was a 30-second flurry from kick-off where Bayern had Arsenal’s penalty area under siege, but Arsenal have controlled the game well since and they have another corner. Odegaard has enjoyed the extra space on offer all game. Arsenal’s captain whips the corner to the back post where Guimaraes was free, but he shins a volley wide.

That makes two goals in three games for Eze. Although he got hooked at half-time in one of them (against Forest on Sunday). It feels like that’s probably how it’s always going to be with a player like him, to be honest. Highs and lows.

Arsenal had to wait for the VAR intervention, but they have the lead in the Allianz thanks to a high-quality goal. Odegaard released Eze in behind with a lovely ball forward, and the former Palace man steadied himself before drilling a left-footed shot across Neuer.

VAR has given it, and Eze strikes Arsenal into the lead at the Allianz 🔥 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/i1LjrZVnbI

Good work from Odgegaard in midfield, one lovely flick to help Arsenal restore some control.

Then Eze puts the ball in the net with a fine finish across Neuer but the flag goes up for offside. This will be checked by VAR... Stanisic, the Bayern left-back, was lingering behind his team-mates on the opposite side of the pitch.

Kane’s range of passing in evidence again, with a driven diagonal over Gabriel’s head towards Saibari but he could not control the ball that was fizzed towards him. Kane is drifting towards the left to open up the pitch for those crossfield passes.

Arsenal caught out on the break by Harry Kane taking a goal kick, from which he picked out Davies with a raking pass down the left. Saibari helped the ball on for Gnabry who was free on the right, but Raya was down quickly to save and Rice cleared.

Arsenal have a corner, after a nice Madueke backheel released Timber. They have the upper hand in this game, but they have lost a major attacking reference with Saka going off. It’s a case of Arsenal’s weakest area being weakened further. From the corner, Calafiori stretches out a leg but directs the ball over.

Arsenal enjoying the lion’s share of possession so far, which is perhaps a reflection of Bayern’s absentees. Kane has just dropped into his own box to receive a pass, and Konsa followed him all the way.

Alphonso Davies runs beyond the Arsenal defence for the first time in the game after Gnabry dribbles past Madueke, but Gabriel made a good challenge from the wrong side.

Ezri Konsa just followed Harry Kane all the way into the Bayern penalty area. Kane loves to drop deep and Arsenal have clearly decided to stick on him, no matter where he goes. For a few moments, Kane was the deepest Bayern player and Konsa was the most advanced Arsenal player.

Havertz has been booked for a foul on Stanisic. Bayern have not been able to build a head of steam as an attacking force so far, but their pressing has forced Arsenal into longer balls forward. No serious chance so far.

So it is now Madueke on the right and Eze on the left for Arsenal. A shame for the spectacle that neither Saka nor Olise are on the pitch, and the Arsenal man had started the game quite brightly.

Saka had a quick chat with Arteta before going down the tunnel. He gestured towards his left quad.

Big problem here for Arsenal: Bukayo Saka has collapsed to the turf after playing a pass, and he looks to have pulled a muscle in his thigh. That is surely his race run tonight, and it looks like he could be out for a few months based on how he went down. Eze is coming on.

The Arsenal fans high up in the Allianz Arena are singing Saka's name as he hobbles off the pitch. He looks very, very uncomfortable. Eze is coming on, so Madueke will move to the right.

Saibari with a cheap loss of possession in midfield, allowing Saka to go straight at the heart of the Bayern defence. He feeds Havertz on the right, but from the German’s cross the ball would not quite drop for Timber or Saka in a crowded box. There looks space on offer for Arsenal. Do they have the speed and quality to exploit it?

Arsenal’s first foray into the attacking third comes from a Raya clip to Timber, pushed well on from right-back, and the defender’s header inside to Saka was a clever one. Madueke received the next pass, but his touch was a little heavy.

Kim players a good switch of play to Laimer, but Calafiori and Rice snuff out any danger and Guimaraes does well to win a midfield foul.

Calafiori was super advanced within the first 30 seconds, straight into an attacking midfield zone. Davies is indeed playing as a left-winger for Bayern in front of Stanisic. In the very early exchanges, Bayern are enjoying more of the ball, but the game still to settle into a pattern.

Arsenal get the game under way, playing in their navy away kit.

The rain continues to lash down. Jurgen Klopp, Germany’s manager, is in the stands having a flim-flam with Rafael Benitez, who has dashed to Bavaria from Anfield where he watched Liverpool vs Villarreal last night.

It seems like Vincent Kompany may have taken a leaf out of Thomas Tuchel’s tactical book. When Arsenal came here in 2024, Tuchel deployed two left-backs on that flank (Mazraoui and Guerreiro) after saying in the press conference that Arsenal’s right-sided attackers were the danger. Kompany appears to have done the same here with Davies, usually a left-back, starting as a winger.

We are going to have to play I expect three or four different games at different stages throughout the game, so we need to have everybody ready to adapt throughout.

Kane has already played against Arsenal since leaving Spurs, so some of the vinegar has gone out of that sub-plot but it is still worth noting that he has scored 15 goals in 22 appearances against them. Several of those goals have been penalties, but Kane is so much more than a goalscorer these days, especially at Bayern where at times he appears to have a free role.

A fascinating aspect of tonight’s game is how Konsa and Gabriel decide to deal with him. Will Arsenal commit to a man-to-man press, with the centre-backs following Kane well beyond the halfway line, or preserve a more zonal approach?

Manchester United are now 4-0 down against a Como team managed by Cesc Fabregas. There is still 15 minutes or more to play. You can follow the rest of the game here to see if they can stem the bleeding.

Will the substitutes again make the difference for Arsenal tonight? In each of their last three league victories, they have won because of goals scored by substitutes. This speaks to the quality of Arteta’s squad, obviously, but also to the Arsenal manager’s ability to pick the right players for the right moments. Over the last year or so, this has become a real strength.

Karl had been expected to replace Olise on the right, but Kompany looks to have stiffened up his midfield by starting Pavlovic, Laimer and Bischof. It will be interesting to see how Saibari and Kane dovetail, two stick-on strikers. It is not Bayern’s strongest team, with Luis Diaz also on the bench.

Bayern Munich starting XI: Neuer, Stanisic, Kim Minjae, Upamecano, Davies, Pavlovic, Laimer, Bischof, Gnabry, Saibari, Kane

Subs: UIreich, Urbig, Ito, Tah, Brown, Luis Diaz, Boey, Sapoko Ndiaye, Karl, Binder

There was little doubt that Arteta would view this game as one that suits Jurrien Timber rather than Ben White. Arsenal’s manager has changed tack by starting Calafiori, who was rested for Arsenal’s first two Champions League games, but Bayern at the Allianz is a significant step up in grade. Madueke rewarded for his showing at Forest.

Arsenal XI: Raya; Timber, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori; Rice, Guimaraes, Odegaard; Saka, Havertz, Madueke

Subs: Kepa, Meslier, White, Mosquera, Lewis-Skelly, Zubimendi Merino, Eze, Gyokeres, Dowman

🔵 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 🟡 Two changes for tonight's test ✊

Vincent Kompany is in the building. It wasn’t clear whether the Bayern head coach would be able to attend tonight’s game because he’s been battling a nasty virus over the last few days. He did not do the usual pre-match press conference yesterday but clearly feels well enough to be here tonight.

In an extract from Sam Dean’s new book on Arsenal’s resurgence under the Spaniard, he reveals that Mike Ashley was keen to bring Arteta to Newcastle United in 2019.

Sam writes: “Arteta also did not have a coaching staff assembled. It is believed that he tried to bring some key individuals on board, such was his interest in accepting Newcastle’s offer, but that the timing was not right for the people he truly wanted. In the end, much to the frustration of Newcastle and Ashley, he said no.”

Arsenal: The Inside Story of Arsenal’s Rebirth Under Mikel Arteta (Pan Macmillan, RRP £22).

This is a proper heavyweight clash but, sadly for the neutrals watching, Bayern are missing some big players. Michael Olise is suspended, Jamal Musiala is injured and Joshua Kimmich is unavailable following the death of his father.

This should all work in Arsenal’s favour, and Mikel Arteta will be looking for a repeat of the energy and quality that his team showed against Bayern last season. Arsenal won 3-1 at the Emirates in November in a performance of real class. It was arguably their most complete showing of the entire campaign.

Ice cold from Martinelli 🥶 https://t.co/uQEHb4x7eH

Some excellent, if disquieting, detail from Sam Dean in this piece about the mood around Arsenal away from the first-team following the news of 60 planned redundancies. Sam writes that there are expecting to be other experienced and influential figures departing. The timing of cuts invites particular scrutiny, coming after the emotional peak of winning the league, record revenues and Mikel Arteta’s new contract.

After Arsenal were beaten by Bayern Munich in a Champions League quarter-final two years ago, Mikel Arteta bemoaned a lack of “magic moments” in attack.

Arsenal have since progressed to a Champions League semi-final and final, while ending a 22-year wait for a Premier League title.

The upward trajectory has translated to tangible success, but Arsenal are still searching the level-raising attacker they lacked on their last visit to the Allianz Arena in 2024.

Back then, Arsenal’s offensive game revolved around Kai Havertz, Bukayo Saka and Martin Odegaard and that remains the case, which makes one wonder if Arsenal’s forward options have been adequately renewed.

A pair of stodgy performances (in victory) against Leeds United and Nottingham Forest have amplified those questions, though some of Arsenal’s slicker football in the season’s early weeks has been forgotten a little hastily.

They have made another strong start to another European campaign with six points from six, but this is undoubtedly their hardest fixture of the league phase.

Their chances of matching last season’s eight wins from eight could well hinge on the outcome of tonight’s game, but there are worse times to face Bayern.

Vincent Kompany’s team looks as formidable as ever, having scored 22 goals from six Bundesliga games so far this season. Their rotational approach is hard to track, with runners from deep breaking beyond Harry Kane who wanders into deep midfield positions.

However, they are without Michael Olise (suspension) and Jamal Musiala (injury) while Joshua Kimmich will miss the game on compassionate grounds following the death of his father.

With the exception of William Saliba, Christos Tzolis and Piero Hincacpie, Arsenal have a pretty clean bill of health and the strength of their bench was crucial against Leeds, Lille and Forest last week.

For Arteta, there are some interesting selection calls to make. It is anticipated that Jurrien Timber will replace Ben White at right-back, and first-choice left-back Riccardo Calafiori has been rested for the Champions League games so far. Should Arteta continue that policy, Myles Lewis-Skelly will fill the position, which will likely mean a midfield start for Bruno Guimarães or Mikel Merino.

Arsenal’s manager must also decide between Noni Madueke and Eberechi Eze on the left, and Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz up front. Havertz is Arteta’s preference, but he also has to consider a relatively short turnaround before Saturday’s league game against Everton.

#1319. Unconventional resistivity reduction in NbP semimetal nanoribbons

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature volume 659, pages 979–986 (2026) Cite this article

Modern and future electronics harbour a key challenge: as conventional metal wires shrink to nanoscale dimensions, their resistivity increases sharply1 owing to surface and grain-boundary scattering. To circumvent this unwanted behaviour, here, we explore the fundamental limits of charge transport in topological semimetal niobium phosphide (NbP) nanoribbons down to approximately 6-nm widths, with industry-friendly top-down nanofabrication. The extracted NbP nanoribbon resistivity reaches 18 ± 4.1 μΩ cm at room temperature with an approximately 9-nm2 cross-sectional area, lower than that of conventional metals and semimetals with comparable size. The NbP nanoribbon resistivity decreases with decreasing width, unlike the classical behaviour of metals such as copper. This trend suggests a growing relative contribution of surface and edge states as the nanoribbon cross-section is reduced, despite a certain amount of disorder, including edge roughness. Our findings advance the understanding of size-dependent transport and scaling in this class of semimetals, offering a platform for nanoscale wires and interconnects in future nanoelectronics.

a, High-angle annular dark-field (HAADF) image of the NbP (1.5 nm) nanoribbon with Nb (3.4 nm) seed layer. The electrically-conducting width of this device is ~12.5 nm. b, Magnified view of the nanocrystalline NbP layer and crystalline Nb seed, together with their corresponding Fast Fourier Transform (FFT), obtained from the boxed regions in panel a. c,d, Bright-field image (c) and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) elemental map (d) of the same device, showing distinct material compositions. In total, three NbP (1.5 nm) nanoribbons were examined by cross-sectional STEM. Across these samples, we observe consistent structural and compositional characteristics, including similar NbP crystallinity and sidewall oxidation, which support the scaling behaviour reported in this work. Additional STEM characterization was not performed on thicker NbP nanoribbons, as the thinnest nanoribbons are most relevant to the main conclusions of this study.

a, HAADF image of the NbP (1.5 nm)/Nb (3.4 nm) nanoribbon with an electrically-conducting width of ~18 nm. b, Magnified view of the nanocrystalline NbP layer and crystalline Nb seed layer, together with their corresponding FFT, obtained from the boxed regions. c,d, Bright-field image (c) and EDS elemental map (d) of the same device, showing distinct material compositions of each region. e, EELS linescan profiles of Nb (blue) and P (red) normalized intensity as a function of position along the direction indicated in panel c. f-h, Representative nanobeam electron diffraction (NBED) patterns extracted from 4D-STEM data at probe positions within the sapphire substrate (f), Nb layer (g), and NbP layer (h), with indexed reflections confirming the distinct crystal structure of each region. i-k, Orientation template matching of the representative NBED pattern in f–h, for the sapphire substrate (i), Nb layer (j) and NbP layer (k). Coloured symbols indicate the local crystallographic orientation of the best-matching template for that pattern. l-n, Phase template matching of the same patterns for the sapphire substrate (l), Nb layer (m) and NbP layer (n).

a, Schematic of the scaling mechanism for conventional metals, with surface scattering and grain boundary scattering. b, As thickness and width of NbP are reduced, the conduction is consistent with the growing dominance of surface carriers, which are disorder-tolerant, with reduced scattering. The total sheet conductance in this case is a sum of the sheet conductance contributed from bulk carriers and surface carriers. c, For thick NbP, bulk carriers dominate the transport, and thus conventional scaling laws apply, with pronounced surface and grain boundary scattering. d, The Fuchs-Sondheimer (FS) and Mayadas-Shatzkes (MS) model fitting of 3.4 nm Nb seed layer, showing an excellent fit. The extracted resistivity with increasing width (W → ∞) is 56.3 μΩ∙cm, which matches the literature results. e, Sheet conductance (GNbP,□) of 1.5 nm NbP as a function of width (red curve), extracted from Fig. 2d of the main text. The sheet conductance from bulk carriers (extracted from Hall measurement) follows the conventional FS-MS scaling model (black dashed line), where the sheet conductance from surface carriers increases as the width decreases due to the increased surface area/volume ratio, as indicated by the purple dashed line. At this ultrathin thickness (1.5 nm), bulk carriers experience strong scattering, resulting in very small bulk carrier sheet conductance. f, GNbP,□ of 10 nm NbP as a function of width (blue curve). At NbP thickness of 10 nm, 3D bulk carriers and 2D top and bottom surface carriers contribute comparably to transport, as shown in Fig. 4b. At this thickness, as the nanoribbon width is reduced, the enhancement in surface conduction is insufficient to offset the increased scattering of bulk carriers. Consequently, bulk transport dominates in this regime, leading to a net reduction of sheet conductance (i.e., increased resistivity) with decreasing width, more similar to conventional metal wires. We note that there could be subtle differences in sidewall roughness and damage in the thicker nanoribbons compared to the thinner ones. See Supplementary Note 2 for the modelling details and more discussion.

a, Bulk Brillouin-zone schematic showing the two mirror planes and nodal rings from the band inversion. b, Representative band dispersion along Γ-S-M’, where the curves calculated without spin-orbit coupling (SOC) show the nodal-ring-related band inversion (plotted in green), and the curves calculated with SOC show the corresponding gap opening (black dashed lines). c, Real-space crystal view highlighting the helical states along the projected mirror line on the surface. d, Surface-state spectrum along \(\overline{\Gamma }\)-\(\overline{{\rm{X}}}\)-\(\overline{\Gamma }\)’, where the narrow Weyl-point window (grey shadow) hosts three pairs of helical states (indicated by arrows) that form the main part of the Fermi arcs, while remnant spin-split surface branches remain visible over a broader energy window (broad green shadow). Blue and red colours indicate the ‘± Sy’ spin polarization at opposite momenta, showing the helical feature. In summary, the narrow Fermi-arc structure is embedded inside a much broader nodal-ring-derived surface-state sector set by the band inversion. See Supplementary Note 7 for more discussion on bulk-topology hierarchy and topological surface-state interpretation.

a, Slab model along the [001] direction for the surface state calculations. Here, the 2 × 2 × 3 supercell is shown as an example. A 4.5 nm thick slab structure of the 1 × 1 × 4 supercell was used in the calculations. b,c, Surface band structures with Nb (b) and P (c) terminations along high-symmetry lines. Blue and red bands indicate the surface states of the Nb and P terminations, respectively. Bulk-projected states shown in pale blue are depicted as the background. The charge neutral point is set to 0 eV. d-f, Surface-projected Fermi surfaces with Nb (upper panels) and P (lower panels) terminations at 0 eV (d), −0.2 eV (e), and −0.4 eV (f). Darker colours represent larger contributions projected from the surface. Weyl points projected on the 2D Brillouin zone are shown as green and purple dots for opposite chirality. The constant energy cuts show surface-dominant open contours over a broad energy window, indicating that Weyl-derived surface bands persist even when the chemical potential is shifted deep into the hole-doped regime, which implies the robustness of the topological surface character. In addition, for the 4.5 nm thick NbP film, the top and bottom surface states exhibit minimal hybridization, except near the Weyl point projections where they meet each other. The Fermi-arc states remain largely unhybridized because they are well separated in momentum space. Even at momenta where they intersect, the resulting hybridization gap is negligible. See Supplementary Note 8 for the modelling details and more discussion.

a, Slab model from the NbP (001) film with thickness d = 1.5 nm and width W = 4.4 to 5.7 nm. b, The one-dimensional (1D) band structure of a W = 5 nm nanoribbon along ky direction. The edge projection is highlighted in purple to show the edge states, while the bulk states are shown in pale blue. Near EF, the edge-projected subbands form an electron-like pocket, consistent with the negative pedge values (panel f). c-e, The spin projection to Sx (c), Sy (d), and Sz (e) components, respectively, for the edge state. The blue and red represent opposite signs of spin polarization. These edge states exhibit a pronounced spin texture arising from strong spin-orbit coupling (SOC) in noncentrosymmetric NbP where Sx and Sz components are locked to the ky momentum in a Rashba-type SOC. This reduces the wavefunction overlap between counter-propagating modes, thereby suppressing the leading backscattering channel, which indicates high-mobility edge conduction. f, The carrier densities from edge (pedge) and 2D film (p2D) are extracted from linear fitting of the total ribbon density (p1D) by p1D = pedge + p2DW, at varying W. Wc denotes the cross-over width at which the edge carrier density would dominate the transport over the top and bottom surface carrier density. Here, Wc ≈ 0 indicates that the enhanced edge conduction of ultrathin films is not primarily driven by an increased edge carrier density. Instead, it is more plausibly attributed to an enhanced carrier mobility arising from reduced backscattering as the edge dimension approaches the quasi-1D limit. See more details in Supplementary Notes 2 and 8. g, Agreement between the nanoribbon fitting (\({p}_{2{\rm{D}}}^{{\rm{NR}}}\)) and that obtained from independent slab film calculations (\({p}_{2{\rm{D}}}^{{\rm{slab}}}\)) which corresponds to the d = 1.5 nm thickness in Supplementary Fig. 10. This agreement supports the self-consistency of our calculations across both the nanoribbon and thin-film geometries.

a, Temperature-dependent effective resistivity (ρeff) of NbP films with different thicknesses up to 90 nm, measured from Hall bar devices. These films have a 3.4 nm Nb seed layer, whose resistivity is measured separately (black symbols). b, Low-temperature limit (2-10 K) of panel a. The smallest superconducting transition temperature Tc (~2.2 K) is in the 3.4 nm Nb layer (black symbols), while higher Tc are observed in the NbP/Nb films, and Tc decreases monotonically with thicker NbP. The symbol colours follow the convention in panel a. c,d, Temperature-dependent sheet conductance (GNbP,□) (c) and resistivity (ρNbP) (d) for all NbP thicknesses, after subtracting the Nb seed contribution. e, ρNbP as a function of NbP thickness at 300 K and 10 K. For comparison, the ρNbP values of nanoribbons with the widest widths (Fig. 2d of the main text) are slightly higher than those from Hall measurements at 300 K, possibly due to process-induced damage during nanofabrication. f, Temperature-dependent ρeff of a ~5 nm-thick Nb control film, measured from a Hall bar device. The residual resistivity ratio (RRR) is 1.48, and the Tc is ~4.2 K. Inset: enlarged view of the low-temperature region. The presence of NbP appears to promote superconductivity in NbP/Nb films. The superconducting proximity effect is one plausible interpretation, although changes in disorder and enhanced inter-grain coupling (in the presence of NbP layer) could also contribute. We also cannot fully rule out the formation of an interfacial superconducting layer at the NbP/Nb interface. The NbP sheet conductance is obtained by subtracting the sheet conductance of the Nb layer (measured independently on control Nb films) from the total sheet conductance of the NbP/Nb stack. The extracted NbP resistivity is then obtained by dividing the NbP thickness by the NbP sheet conductance, i.e. ρNbP = dNbP/GNbP,□, where GNbP,□ = Gtot,□ - GNb,□ and Gtot,□ = dtot/ρeff, where Gtot,□ is the total sheet conductance of the NbP/Nb stack, dtot is the total stack thickness and ρeff is the measured effective resistivity (panel a). The GNbP,□ (panel c) represents the NbP sheet conductance after subtracting the independently-measured Nb seed contribution. Additional validation of the subtraction method using Pt/Nb stacks is provided in Supplementary Fig. 19. Control experiments using Pt/Nb stacks validate that the subtraction procedure itself does not generate an anomalous resistivity trend. Nevertheless, the conductance of the Nb seed layer within NbP/Nb stacks cannot be independently measured and it cannot be said, with absolute certainty, that its behaviour is identical to that of the separately measured Nb control film. Thus, the extracted NbP resistivity relies, by necessity, on the model used.

a-c, Hall resistance (Rxy) vs. magnetic field (B) measured at various temperatures for 3.4 nm Nb (a), 1.5 nm NbP (b), and 10 nm NbP (c). For the NbP films (b,c), the Nb seed layer contribution is subtracted at each corresponding temperature to extract NbP Hall response, using the same two-layer Hall conduction model described in the supplement. d, Effective three-dimensional carrier density (p3D) for all films, revealing opposite temperature-dependence: ultrathin 1.5 nm NbP shows an increasing p3D upon cooling, whereas both thicker NbP (10 nm) and Nb (3.4 nm) display decreasing p3D. (This figure is also included in the main text as Fig. 4d and is reproduced here for convenience). e, Effective hole mobility (μp) of the same films vs. temperature. NbP films exhibit a pronounced increase in mobility upon cooling due to suppressed phonon scattering, whereas the 3.4 nm Nb film shows only a slight rise in mobility, indicating that its transport remains strongly limited by surface scattering.

a-c, Longitudinal sheet resistance (Rxx) vs. magnetic field (B) measured at various temperatures for films of Nb seed layer (3.4 nm) (a), for NbP (1.5 nm) on the Nb seed (b), and for NbP (10 nm) on the Nb seed (c). All measurements were performed with the magnetic field applied perpendicular to the film plane and current direction. At low temperatures, all films exhibit a pronounced negative cusp near low field regions, arising from the interplay of superconducting fluctuations and weak antilocalization. d-e, Longitudinal sheet resistance (Rxx) vs. magnetic field (B) measured at 1.8 K for both 1.5 nm thick NbP (on 3.4 nm Nb seed layer) and for the Nb layer (3.4 nm) evaluated separately. Measurements were performed with B field perpendicular to the film plane and current direction (d), and with B applied in-plane (e). The superconducting transition temperatures are Tc ~ 6 K for the 1.5 nm NbP (on Nb) and ~2.2 K for the 3.4 nm Nb film (see Fig. 3d of the main text). The upper critical field Hc2, defined as the midpoint between the normal state resistance and zero resistance, is extracted. At 1.8 K, the out-of-plane critical field \({H}_{c2}^{\perp }\) is 2.2 T for NbP (1.5 nm) and 0.38 T for Nb (3.4 nm). The in-plane critical field at 1.8 K exceeds 9 T for NbP (1.5 nm) and reaches 4.44 T for Nb (3.4 nm). The superconducting coherence length estimates are provided in the supplement. The sense current used for Hall bar measurements is 0.5 mA, corresponding to a current density of ~0.1 MA/cm2 for the NbP (1.5 nm) film and ~0.15 MA/cm2 for the 3.4 nm Nb control, with the same 100 μm Hall bar device width. We note that this sense current is well below the superconducting critical current: even when we increased the sense current up to 10 mA, we were unable to suppress the superconducting state at 1.8 K.

a, Cross-sectional HAADF STEM image of the alternating NbP/Nb multilayers grown on sapphire. b-d, Denoised nanobeam electron diffraction (NBED) patterns extracted from 4D-STEM data for all Nb layers (Nb layers 1-3) showing consistent body-centred cubic (bcc) diffraction symmetry with indexed reflections, confirming crystalline quality across all Nb layers. Scale bars: 0.5 Å−1. e, EDS line scan across the multilayer stack showing Nb (blue), P (red), and Al (light brown) as a function of position, integrated over a ~ 5nm wide region along the direction indicated by the yellow arrow in panel a, confirming periodic composition and abrupt elemental transitions at each NbP/Nb interface. f-h, denoised NBED patterns from NbP layers 1–3, displaying diffraction symmetry consistent with the NbP crystal structure with indexed reflections, consistent with uniform phase and crystallographic orientation throughout the multilayer stack. The diffraction spots become progressively broader from layer 1 to layer 3, suggesting a gradual decrease in crystalline coherence in NbP layers further from the substrate. This is further supported by the emergence of diffuse ring features in the Layer 3 diffraction pattern, indicative of increasing structural disorder.

#1318. Bruno Fernandes opens door to Sporting return amid doubts over Man United future as captain insists 'now is not the time' to discuss new contract

Published: 17:50 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 17:54 EST, 24 November 2026

Bruno Fernandes has left the door open for a return to Sporting Lisbon amid increasing uncertainty over his future at Manchester United.

Fernandes was a fans’ favourite at Sporting before joining United in January 2020 in a deal worth up to £68million.

The United captain has become equally popular at Old Trafford, but returned to Lisbon on Tuesday night with a question mark hanging over his next move after talks over a new contract stalled.

Fernandes’ current deal is due to run out at the end of June – and he will be able to speak to foreign clubs from January 1 – although United are expected to trigger an automatic 12-month extension to prevent him from leaving as a free agent in the summer.

Asked if he would consider a move back to the Jose Alvalade Stadium, where United meet Sporting in the Champions League on Wednesday night, Fernandes said: ‘I will never close the door to Sporting. It will always be a club with a special place in my heart.

‘Sporting was the first club that believed in my potential. I’ve always felt here from the fans – regardless of what may have happened – all the love and kindness from them, and that was essential to make me grow as a player.’

Bruno Fernandes has rejected two offers of a new contract to extend his stay at Man United

On his future at Old Trafford, Fernandes insisted that he wants to focus on turning United’s season around after they slipped into the relegation zone and replaced head coach Michael Carrick with Mauricio Pochettino.

‘We have time to speak about that,’ said Fernandes. ‘I know it's my future and I probably shouldn't look that way because I haven't got long left, but I'm more worried about results.

‘Contract talks have stopped for us to start winning games, and then we can talk about a contract. Now is not the moment.’

#1317. The two things Roberto De Zerbi demanded from Luca Williams-Barnett's first Tottenham start as 18-year-old star signs new lucrative deal, writes MATT BARLOW

Published: 08:08 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 18:17 EST, 24 November 2026

Having summoned Luca Williams-Barnett to his office to let the teenager know he would be making his first Premier League start, Roberto De Zerbi could not resist a little bit of fun.

De Zerbi cast a serious demeanour and told him he had weighed the options and figured the best course of action would be 60 minutes with the Under-21s.

Williams-Barnett did not hide his disappointment. 'Why, do you think you are ready to start for the first team?' asked the Spurs boss. The 18-year-old said he thought so.

De Zerbi cracked a smile and told him he was in the team against Ipswich but demanded two things in return.

First, that his young star would play with freedom as though 'in the park with friends' and second that he would work without the ball in the manner of the world's best players in his position, such as Lamine Yamal.

This is where the comparisons to Yamal emerged soon after Williams-Barnett lit up the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. On Tuesday, he was rewarded for his progress with a new contract at the club.

He said: 'This is a special moment for me and my family, and one I have worked really hard to reach. But this is only the start.

Luca Williams-Barnett scored his first Premier League goal for Tottenham on his first start in the top flight

The talented academy youngster may not be lightning fast but he has pace and creates goals

'Spurs is a family to me. I've been here for so long – it's a second home, where I trust the people and coaches who have pushed me to become the player I am today.

'The club has trusted and believed in me, now I'm ready to repay that.'

Hopes are indeed high. Similarities with Yamal are evident in physique, his fluency of movement on the ball and the bursts of pace, the way they look to play. Even the hairstyle.

Just as Yamal, a left footer, likes to operate wide on the right for Barcelona and Spain, De Zerbi deployed Williams-Barnett as a right footer on the left, although most of his youth career has been spent centrally in the No 10 position.

He does not possess what you would consider in modern football to be exceptional pace, but he is quick, and his strengths are on the ball. He likes the ball. He creates. And he scores goals.

From wide on the left against Ipswich, he scored within 15 minutes, darting in at the back post to finish, and created the second for Dominic Solanke, with a 60-yard run from inside his own half and cross with his left foot.

His brilliance lit up the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, where there has not been a lot to celebrate in the last 18 months. Terrible home form was the crux of last season's relegation fears.

Here, they rose to salute a new talent, one of their own. One De Zerbi believes has the attitude to match his outrageous talent. Confident, certainly. Aware of his natural gifts and his technical skills. Perhaps bordering on arrogance when on the pitch.

De Zerbi was pleased to see Williams-Barnett, in a seat nearby on the team bus from the training ground to the stadium, watching YouTube clips of Ronaldinho, Eden Hazard and Neymar.

The Spurs boss, who has faith in the power of inspirational video footage, took this as a positive sign. The youngster was relaxed but more than this he had a passion for football and always looking to learn.

'I'm positive about his character and behaviour because I've been working with him for three or four months and I know him enough,' said De Zerbi, whose tactical instructions involved James Maddison operating closely to Williams-Barnett, a kindred spirit in a footballing sense able to talk him through the game.

When the teenager set off on the swaggering run for Solanke's goal, Maddison could be seen nearby urging him forward into the ocean of space left open by Ipswich.

The 18-year-old had rival clubs circling but Spurs have now tied him down

Born and raised in Luton, Williams-Barnett comes from a strong, grounded family - which will only help as he looks to assimilate into the senior side

Spurs have prioritised Premier League experience in the transfer market under De Zerbi to create a more mature dressing room environment. Signings such as Andy Robertson have been key to this.

The policy is not purely for the benefit of academy graduates stepping into the first-team environment, but it does help when it comes to setting the standards required in elite sport.

Anyone gifted enough to break into the Spurs squad will have been feted as a star through the youth development phase and well rewarded to resist others trying to lure them away.

Williams-Barnett was under contract until 2028 but his new deal means clubs circling must now look elsewhere.

It is easy for impressionable teens to become conceited in this situation. Williams-Barnett has had discipline and time-keeping issues but most at Spurs speak of a young man devoted to his football from a strong, loving family who are sure to keep him grounded.

He was born and raised in Luton, starting out in Luton Town's pre-academy to Under 10s, before Spurs paid a small fee for him.

His father Jonathan Barnett was a central midfielder in Step Three of non-league football, known as 'Jono' and playing for various clubs in the region including Dunstable Town and Arlesey Town and renowned for his passing, set pieces and with an eye for goal.

Although more of a dribbler, Luca grew up with football in the family, polishing his technical skills with his dad in the back garden. 'He is from a very good family and it's crucial for this type of players,' said De Zerbi.

Spurs have been here before, of course, with talented teens breaking through with N17 at their feet.

There was Mikey Moore's wonderful cameo against AZ Alkmaar after which Ange Postecoglou called for patience and commonsense, and Maddison went on TV and said it was 'like having Neymar on the left wing'.

There was Jose Mourinho taking the match ball from Son Heung-min, who had just scored the most incredible solo goal against Burnley, and handing it to Troy Parrott on his Premier League debut.

There was Mauricio Pochettino dubbing Marcus Edwards his 'mini Messi'. Pochettino soon came to wish he had not burdened Edwards with such lavish praise.

The pitfalls are well known and progress is rarely a smooth upward trajectory. It is a balancing act between maximising potential and getting carried away.

De Zerbi is quietly confident Williams-Barnett has what it takes to handle the hype.

On the new deal, thought to be for five years, the manager said: 'Luca is a player I think the world of, and I'm so happy that he has signed a new contract.

'He has benefitted from being around the first team every day, growing in stature and consistency, and has deserved his place in the matchday squad over recent weeks.

'Everyone can see how technically gifted Luca is on the pitch but I also love his calmness and decision-making under pressure.

'The best players have confidence on the pitch and humility off it. There is still plenty of room for Luca to improve, and I know he will continue to work hard every day to be the best version of himself.'

#1316. Florian Wirtz opens up on chats with ex-Liverpool boss Jurgen Klopp and thanks Andoni Iraola after starring role in Man United thrashing

Published: 18:12 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 18:24 EST, 24 November 2026

Florian Wirtz has thanked Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola for sparking his resurgence and insists he never stopped believing in himself.

The German arrived with a big reputation when he completed a £116million move from Bayer Leverkusen but has been a constant punchbag for critics after failing to reach the heights that saw him win the Bundesliga title as the league’s star man.

Wirtz, though, has been much improved this year and put in his best performance for the Reds on Sunday in the 4-0 thumping of Manchester United And he insists Iraola – and old Anfield boss Jurgen Klopp – are the reason.

‘I am really enjoying playing under him,’ said Wirtz on Iraola, who replaced Arne Slot in the summer. ‘He is a really good coach. He has shown that his whole career as a manager.

‘He is bringing me back to the place where I was maybe two years ago where I played really good football.

‘I can feel that he gives me confidence and I am really happy about that. I am just trying to give him back what he gives me. I am really happy with that.’

Florian Wirtz has opened up on talking to ex-Liverpool boss Jurgen Klopp after finally hitting form for Liverpool

Wirtz won man of the match in Liverpool's 4-0 thrashing of Manchester United on Sunday

Wirtz has also had the added influence of Klopp, now Germany boss, in recent months. He said: ‘We always speak about Liverpool when we have the time to do so. He had a great time here. He is the coach who stayed here the most of his career.

‘He just tells me all the time that he loved his time here, the people love him here, he tries to give me some advice to get successful over here because he has shown how it is done.

'He knows a lot about this club, a lot of people here, he can give me some good advice.’

Wirtz added: ‘It's not about the people who talk about me. It's the goals I set myself and the performances I want to show for myself.

‘I always believed in myself. I knew my qualities and I know them now. Sometimes there are phases where you have to work even more to get the output, but I'm just enjoying the moment and really happy at the moment that it's going well. I'm happy with myself.’

Meanwhile, Cody Gakpo will miss the Merseyside derby with a calf problem and fellow Dutchman Ryan Gravenberch is also in a race against time to be fit for the trip to Everton due to a fascia issue. Neither have travelled to Belgium for Liverpool’s clash against Club Brugge.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of this Europa League tie between Bournemouth and AC Milan at the Vitality Stadium.

Back in 2008, Bournemouth’s prospect of a European meeting with Milan seemed impossible. After entering administration with crippling debts of around £4m, Bournemouth were handed a 10-point deduction and relegated from League One. To make matters worse, a hefty 17-point deduction was given to the club ahead of the 2008-09 League Two season, with relegation to non-league seeming inevitable. However, midway through the campaign, the transformative Eddie Howe was parachuted in as Bournemouth’s saviour, eventually guiding the club to safety.

Fast forward to October 2026 in an extraordinary rise and Bournemouth are competing in their first-ever European campaign in the club’s 127-year existence. They welcome Milan to Dorset, having earned back-to-back victories over Real Sociedad and Sturm Graz to kick off their inaugural Europa League adventure in style.

Now, they host the second most successful side in the European Cup history. In terms of heritage and silverware, these clubs could not be further apart, but on the pitch, it’s incredibly tough to call.

On Sunday, Marco Rose’s Bournemouth picked up their first Premier League win of the season, beating 10-man Sunderland 2-0 at the Vitality thanks to goals from Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson to move out of the relegation zone.

Meanwhile, Ruben Amorim is in charge at Milan and returns to England after a tumultuous 14-month reign at Manchester United, where he was sacked in January. Milan lost their opening Europa League fixture 2-0 at home to Benfica, before battering Salzburg 4-0 in Austria, with Alphadjo Cisse netting a stunning hat-trick.

Crystal Palace are also in the Europa League tonight and face an incredibly daunting away trip to Turkish side Besiktas. Pressure is firmly on manager Pierre Sage following the 5-0 humiliation against Brighton last weekend and a shaky start to the season. Palace lost 3-2 to Sage’s former employers Lyon in their previous Europa League outing, with a positive performance and result needed to restore the fans’ faith.

Both games kick-off at 20:00, with team news coming imminently.

Tottenham Hotspur striker Richarlison is reportedly keen on returning to Everton, with the Brazilian international considering a reunion with his former club ahead of the January transfer window.

The 29-year-old has endured a frustrating spell in north London and appears increasingly likely to seek a fresh challenge after falling out of favour under manager Roberto De Zerbi.

According to a Sky Sports report, Richarlison would welcome the chance to return to Everton, where he previously established himself as a key attacking player.

The Merseyside outfit attempted to bring the forward back during the summer transfer window, but an agreement between the two clubs and the player could not be completed.

Everton manager David Moyes could now have another chance to strengthen his attacking options with a January deal.

Richarlison has struggled to establish himself at Tottenham following his £60m move from Goodison Park in 2022. His situation has grown more complicated after the club excluded him from the Premier League squad for the current campaign.

The Brazilian has also been training away from the senior setup, making a departure increasingly appealing as he looks to secure regular first-team football.

Everton could face competition from clubs outside England, with interest emerging from Turkey and Saudi Arabia.

Richarlison previously scored 53 goals in 152 appearances for the Toffees, showing he can make an impact in the Premier League.

His familiarity with Everton and the chance to work under Moyes again could make a return particularly attractive.

Nevertheless, his considerable wages and recent lack of competitive action could complicate negotiations between the two clubs.

#1313. Derek McInnes urges his Rangers side to stop switching off after edging out Aberdeen in thriller

Published: 18:37 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 18:42 EST, 24 November 2026

Derek McInnes last night hit out at his dozy Rangers side for switching off in the latter stages of a hard-fought 3-2 home win over Aberdeen and warned them they will be made to pay over the course of the season if they carry on being so naive.

Goals from Ryan Naderi, Djeidi Gassama and Raskin in the first ten minutes of the second half put the Ibrox outfit in total command after Brad Lyons had put the visitors a goal up at the break.

However, Findlay Marshall made it a nervy finish for Rangers after scoring for the Dons on 58 minutes and it took a brilliant save from keeper Ivor Pandur to deny Nicky Devlin before Rangers saw it out to take their unbeaten run to 14 games and close the gap on Celtic at the head of the Premiership to just one point.

‘I am relieved to win,’ said manager McInnes, who made three changes and altered the shape at the interval. ‘I thought we only played with the intelligence, speed and intensity for about 20 minutes and, in that period, showed how good we can be.

‘But we put the game at risk. We lost a cheap goal and weren’t aggressive enough. We lost two goals, really, from set-plays.

‘At 3-1 up against a team as game as Aberdeen were — and they were really good value — our naivety for the second goal is beyond me.

Rangers boss Derek McInnes was relieved to win but urges his side to keep focused

Nicolas Raskin slots home the third goal for Rangers in their thrilling 3-2 win over Aberdeen

‘I am not sure it was a free-kick in the first place, but we turn our backs. It is almost as if we are in a daydream and we allow them to manipulate the ball. Great finish from wee Findlay Marshall, but we put ourselves in the mire there by just knocking off.

‘We were so naive at times in the game. We scored good goals at good times but I still think Aberdeen will be disappointed not to get something.

‘We should have stayed in charge of the game and the second goal we lose allows Aberdeen to keep going with a bit of oxygen and carry a threat. I am disappointed with the lack of control in the game and I am not really happy with a lot of what we saw.

‘That has to change because we will not always be able to outscore the opposition.

‘We hit Aberdeen like a train in the second half and they found themselves 3-1 down because of the quality and intelligence of our play. For whatever reason, we then started playing back the way again. We played more passbacks to my goalkeeper than I can remember in a long time.

‘We need to play forward and show more control in the game. I am looking for better from my team.’

Raskin, meanwhile, has urged his Rangers team-mates to blast themselves to the top of the table on Saturday night and really pile the pressure on arch-rivals Celtic.

The Light Blues play host to third-placed Falkirk on Saturday afternoon with Celtic going to Hearts the following day and the Belgian midfielder wants to make sure they don’t let the defending champions off the hook the way they have in previous years.

‘We need to keep it going,’ said Raskin. ‘In recent years, we have not been able to put enough pressure on the other team and now we are doing it, so that is good.

‘We will see how everybody reacts after next Saturday.’

Djeidi Gassama scored to complete a stunning turaround for Rangers early in the second half

Raskin has also revealed it took a stern half-time team talk from manager McInnes along with those substitutions to spark his side into life after a dreadful first-half performance.

‘I think we made the game hard for ourselves in the first half,’ said the Belgian. ‘The manager had an honest discussion in the dressing room and we came back and scored two early goals, which helped. But we weren’t focused enough after the third goal and conceded to make it even harder.

‘We showed character again. The manager said what a manager has to say when you are losing, playing badly, you are 1-0 down and you have to win the game.’

Aberdeen boss Mario Frick left Ibrox feeling his side had missed a real opportunity.

‘I am disappointed with the five or six minutes after half-time. That hurts,’ he said.

‘We saw a good performance, Rangers were beatable tonight.

‘We need more time. We have to improve. We have to talk about those ten minutes. After 3-1 down, we came back and we believed in ourselves. We deserved an equaliser.’

#1312. Disturbances and climate drive tree elevational shifts
